our_argument_summary: WIN-046 (verdict Self-Contradicted): S2=12.00h is the model input (SOLAR_H/2), not a derived output; the dome local sun cannot produce the observed two-bulge semidiurnal pattern; and the amplitude hierarchy is inverted (dome daily-pulse mechanism predicts S1>S2 by Fourier decomposition, observation gives S2>>S1). Post-hoc/trivial-transcription framing in detail_verdict_text.

holes_found.description: NEW NUMERICAL INCONSISTENCY INTRODUCED BY THE c5 PATCH: two of the four named station ratios do not match our own EXP-581 sourcing. The patched prose states 'Pugh 1987 Table 4.2; ... Brest 27:1, Plymouth 17:1, Newlyn 26:1, San Francisco 17:1'. EXP-581 quantitative_verification.s2_s1_ratio_at_mid_lat lists the underlying Pugh 1987 Table 4.2 values as Newlyn S2=0.51 m / S1=0.04 m -> 13:1 and San Francisco S2=0.21 m / S1=0.022 m -> 9.5:1. So published Newlyn (26:1) is ~2x the table-derived value and San Francisco (17:1) is ~1.8x. Brest (0.65/0.024=27:1) and Plymouth (0.50/0.03=17:1) match exactly. Because the prose attributes these to a NAMED table (Pugh 1987 Table 4.2), a reader can look it up and find the discrepancy, which damages citation discipline more than an unsourced number would. The argument (S2>>S1 at mid-latitudes) is unaffected — both stations are still strongly S2-dominant — so severity is moderate, not major, but it should be corrected.
holes_found.recommendation: Replace the two wrong ratios with the EXP-581 table-derived values: Newlyn 13:1, San Francisco ~9.5:1. Since SF 9.5:1 then falls just below the stated bound (see hole 1), cleanest fix is either (a) drop San Francisco and list Brest 27:1, Plymouth 17:1, Newlyn 13:1 (all >=13:1, consistent with ~10:1 or greater), or (b) reframe as a range: 'S2:S1 ratios from ~9.5:1 (San Francisco) to 27:1 (Brest) across mid-latitude coastal stations'. Option (b) is most faithful to EXP-581 and harder to call cherry-picked. If a specific Pugh 1987 printing genuinely lists 26:1 / 17:1, update EXP-581 to match and cite the page — but the analyst compilation says otherwise, so (a)/(b) are the defensible path.

holes_found.description: CONSISTENCY TENSION RECREATED. Correcting San Francisco to its EXP-581 value (9.5:1) puts a named station just below the prose bound '~10:1 or greater' — the exact prose-vs-station mismatch c5 hole 1 flagged for the old 4:1 bound. The c5 patch avoided this only by carrying the (incorrect) 17:1 SF figure. Whatever fix is applied to hole 0 must keep the named-station list internally consistent with the stated bound.
holes_found.recommendation: Adopt hole-0 option (a) (drop SF, keep stations >=13:1) or option (b) (state a range and remove the single-sided lower-bound phrasing). Do not keep a '~10:1 or greater' lower bound while listing a sub-10:1 station.

stronger_arguments.description: The S2/S1 inversion case is strongest framed as a range with the bound matching the weakest mid-latitude station shown, rather than a single lower bound plus illustrative stations — it pre-empts both the cherry-picking objection (EXP-581 anticipated_objections.2) and the prose/station mismatch. EXP-581 itself notes the literature is MORE favourable than the conservative framing (honest_correction_to_curmudgeon), so a faithful range loses no rhetorical force.

kernel_of_truth.description: The c5 patch round was substantively correct on 3 of 4 holes and the new prose is genuinely stronger than the pre-patch text (data/wins.json:WIN-046.detail_evidence). The Fourier qualifier 'asymmetric, non-degenerate' (data/wins.json:WIN-046.detail_evidence) precisely closes the even-symmetric counterexample c5 raised, and dropping Honolulu under the mid-latitude qualifier is defensible because tropical stations have anomalously large radiational S1 (EXP-581.json:anticipated_objections.2.response).
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Patch quality on the qualitative argument does not excuse the two transcription errors in the named ratios (data/wins.json:WIN-046.detail_evidence vs EXP-581.json:quantitative_verification.s2_s1_ratio_at_mid_lat). A numeric claim tied to a checkable named table (Pugh 1987 Table 4.2) must match that table; otherwise the same citation-discipline objection c5 hole 0 raised about the unsourced 0.10 m figure reappears in a new form.

deeper_analysis: Verification scope was the c5 patch set (queue 478, class verification). Outcome: 3 of 4 c5 holes cleanly closed and correct; the 4th (station-list rewrite) closed the original problem but introduced a sibling of the same class. This is the patch counter-argument the operator accepted in curmudgeon.md Step 8a playing out in miniature — a verification re-review surfacing a patch-introduced error rather than rubber-stamping. The verdict (Self-Contradicted) was not re-litigated this cycle: affirmed at c5 (current_verdict_holds true) and out of scope for a patch-verification pop; I note only that the label leans on trivial/post-hoc + physical-refutation reasoning more than on an explicit cross-WIN self-contradiction, which a future holistic pass could examine. No verdict change recommended now.
summary_for_decider: VERIFICATION RESULT for queue 478 / WIN-046 c5 patches: PASS-WITH-ONE-NEW-HOLE. ISS-2564 (S1 0.10->0.03), ISS-2565 (4:1->~10:1 bound + Fourier narrowing), ISS-2566 (wrong sign->wrong direction) all verified closed and correct. NEW moderate hole: the station-list patch lists Newlyn 26:1 and San Francisco 17:1 attributed to Pugh 1987 Table 4.2, but EXP-581 derives Newlyn 13:1 and SF 9.5:1 from that same table (Brest 27:1 and Plymouth 17:1 match). Recommend a minor-prose ISS to correct both; cleanest is to drop SF and list Brest 27:1 / Plymouth 17:1 / Newlyn 13:1 (all consistent with the ~10:1-or-greater bound), or reframe as a 9.5:1-27:1 range. Minor companion hole: corrected SF (9.5:1) would otherwise dip below the stated lower bound, so fix bound and stations together. Verdict holds; no verdict change.
